newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds marked down as players keep to sidelines.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds marked down as players keep to sidelines.

text.p: Irish bonds were marked down in line with other markets on Friday, with trade volume down to a bare minimum ahead of a weekend G7 meeting and political uncertainty, dealers said.

"It's been a quiet day at the end of a quiet week," a dealer said. "With two general elections coming up (in Britain and France) and this weekend's G7 meeting investors are keeping to the sidelines, but it's par for the course to see a bear market ahead of elections."

By 1500 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 20 pence from Thursday's close at 101.65 to yield 6.05 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 fell 30 pence to 108.00 to yield 6.80 percent.

Dealers said Irish bonds were yielding 146 basis points over German bunds in the five-year area - a widening of three basis points from Thursday - and 89 basis points over bunds in the 10-year, a narrowing of one basis point.
European bonds continued to slide on Friday as markets worried about the chances of European monetary union and eyed weakness in U.S. T-bonds.

Overnight comments from Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer that the U.S. economy was growing too fast and that the Japanese Ministry of Finance had ordered Nissan Mutual Life Insurance Co to halt its operations, also hurt sentiment.

At home, there was no market reaction to Central Statistics Office figures which showed that the value of Irish retail sales fell a provisional 0.9 percent in February, giving a year-on-year rise of 5.8 percent.

UK gilts meanwhile, renewed declines as data showed British quarterly GDP rose 1.0 percent, and 3.0 percent on the year against a forecast of 0.9 in the quarter, and 2.9 on the year. -- Kevin Smith, Dublin newsroom + 353 1 661 3377
